requirements.statement: In each data table, each element with role="rowheader" or role="columnheader" whose content applies to the whole row or the whole column has role="rowheader" if it is a row header, or role="columnheader" if it is a column header.

citations.quote: Pour chaque balise pourvue d’un attribut WAI-ARIA `role="rowheader"` ou `role="columnheader"` dont le contenu s’applique à la totalité de la ligne ou de la colonne, la balise vérifie-t-elle une de ces conditions ?

routes.statement: The element is a row header and has role="rowheader".

routes.statement: The element is a column header and has role="columnheader".

citations.quote: La balise possède un attribut WAI-ARIA `role="columnheader"` pour les en-têtes de colonne.
Soit un attribut WAI-ARIA `role="columnheader"` pour les en-têtes de colonne.

rationale.text: One requirement with two routes, each tied to a kind of header: role="rowheader" for a row header, role="columnheader" for a column header. The role is an attribute that code can read; which kind of header an element is, and whether it applies to the whole row or column, are not. A header is a cell whose content serves as the label of all or part of its row or column, so an element with role="columnheader" fails only if it is in fact a row header, and its position in the grid does not prove that. An element whose header covers only a part of its row or column is outside this test (test 5.6.3 applies to it). Whether a structure is a data table rather than a layout table is judgment too (see 5.1.1). So no element is surely in scope with a sure fault, and the entry is none. No axe rule is tagged for this test, so there are no links. Applicability is judgment. Needs holds assistive_tech: these roles are often used in ARIA tables, and the glossary counts an element with role="table" as a data table only when assistive technologies render it correctly.
